case.source_text:
Synthetic nurse note for software testing. No real patient data.

The driver restarted blood-pressure treatment ten days ago after running out of tablets and now describes brief grey vision and a swaying sensation when stepping down from the cab; he says he stays aware throughout, but a coworker recalls him leaning against the vehicle without answering immediately. One event followed a long period without food, another occurred after breakfast, and there is no witness account detailed enough to establish whether either episode involved loss of consciousness.

An urgent-care note from last winter records Persistent BP 178/104 mmHg before treatment, while today's seated BP 146/88 mmHg was taken once and a pharmacy receipt from three days earlier shows 154/92 without documenting the rest period or cuff size. The driver reports no chest pain, says his father had a myocardial infarction, and has no personal cardiac diagnosis documented in the material supplied.

He is unsure whether the new tablets caused the symptoms or whether the episodes began before the prescription change; he has not completed four weeks on the current regimen, has no standing measurements and has not brought the proposed cardiology review. The nurse records unresolved symptoms and inconsistent timing rather than a confirmed medication adverse effect, persistent current pressure or a diagnosed cause of collapse.
